subject: Audit & Access Logs — retention windows, exports, and deletion process
messages:
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: Acme Corp Security <security@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick Q on audit/access log retention & exports

Hi Rishi,

We're working through our compliance checklist for a pilot and need a crisp summary of Redwood's current behavior for audit and access logs. Specifically:

- What are the default retention windows for (1) access logs (authn/authorization/connection events) and (2) audit logs (configuration changes, admin actions)?
- Can we export raw logs (including timestamps, actor, action, resource, and request IDs) on demand? Formats? Delivery targets (S3/GCS/CSV/JSON)?
- Is there an automated deletion workflow we can trigger for specific tenants (e.g., we need 90-day deletion for one environment)?
- Do logs ever contain customer input (payload) or only metadata/IDs?

We need this to complete our internal risk review. If you can point me at a short spec or attach a sample export, that would help a lot.

Thanks,
Jane
Jane Doe
Security Engineer, Acme Corp

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q on audit/access log retention & exports

Hi Jane — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then a couple of notes plus attachments.

Summary:
- Access logs (connection/auth events): default retention 90 days for Hosted.
- Audit logs (admin/config changes): default retention 365 days for Hosted; Dedicated/Private customers can configure longer/shorter retention via policy.
- Exports: yes — ad hoc and scheduled exports supported. Formats: JSON (structured), CSV (flattened). Delivery: S3, GCS, Azure Blob, or console download; we also provide a streaming API for near-real-time delivery.
- Deletion: tenant-scoped deletion APIs and scheduled retention policies exist for Dedicated/Private. For Hosted, we support scheduled retention (e.g., set 90d) and manual deletion requests via support ticket for special cases.
- Payloads: logs do not store plain customer inputs. We log metadata and identifiers (request_id, user_id hashed/pseudonymized).

Attached: audit_log_spec_sheet.pdf (high-level fields exported) and export_instructions_v1.md (console/API steps).

A couple of caveats:
- For Hosted customers, very short retention (<30 days) or deletion-for-DSR requests require Legal/Security review — we typically validate scope and retention timeline before executing a manual purge.
- For Dedicated/Private, customers can pin retention and we provide tools to run on-demand exports to your cloud bucket without Redwood staging the data.

If you'd like, Monica can run a quick demo of the export flow into your S3 sandbox and Neha can confirm the data minimization guarantees.

Next steps: do you want a 30-minute walkthrough tomorrow?

Best,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 6 May 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q on audit/access log retention & exports

Thanks Rishi — happy to help. A couple practical notes that might be useful for Acme: 

- If you want to try an export yourself: Console -> Observability -> Audit Logs -> Export -> Choose format (JSON recommended) -> Destination (S3/GCS/Azure). We also support specifying a time window and filtering by actor or resource.
- For scheduled delivery, set up an export job (cron-like) and provide an IAM role for S3/GCS; we do the writes directly into your bucket.
- For Hosted accounts where we need to perform a manual deletion, please open the support ticket with the tenant ID + exact UTC window and we will coordinate with Security.

I've dropped a short playbook in the shared drive here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD_example_export_playbook — it includes example curl commands for the streaming API.

If you want, I can start an export to the sandbox bucket Acme gave us (if you confirm the bucket name and role).

Cheers,
Monica
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>
To: monica_patel@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: Acme Corp Security <security@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 6 May 2026 10:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q on audit/access log retention & exports

Monica — that playbook link is exactly what we needed. Thank you.

We can provide an S3 bucket (acme-logs-pilot) and an IAM role. I'll confirm bucket details in a separate secure note.

Two follow-ups for Neha/Redwood Security: 
- For compliance, we need written confirmation that exported audit logs never contain raw customer prompts/inputs.
- For the deletion workflow: if we request a tenant-scoped purge (90-day window), what is the typical SLA and what evidence do you provide once deletion is complete?

If it's easier, we can hop on a short call tomorrow.

Best,
Jane

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 7 May 2026 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q on audit/access log retention & exports

Hi Jane — Neha from Security here. Quick confirmations and suggested artifacts: 

1) Data minimization: Redwood audit and access logs contain metadata (timestamps, request_id, status codes, actor identifiers). We do not log full customer prompt/response payloads as part of audit/access logs. If a customer enables additional request logging for debugging (opt-in), that is gated and documented; otherwise, payloads are not included.

2) Exported log contents: Exports include the fields listed in the attached spec; PII is not included by default. Identifiers are pseudonymized (SHA-256 truncated) where necessary. If Acme has specific PII concerns, we can work through a mapping/filters before export.

3) Deletion workflow and evidence: For Hosted tenants, we provide the following process for a tenant-scoped purge: 
   - Customer opens a support request with tenant_id and UTC time range.
   - Security performs scope validation and schedules the purge (typically within 3–5 business days for standard requests).
   - After purge, we provide a signed deletion report (timestamped audit showing objects removed and storage paths), plus an export of the deletion job logs for your records.

For Dedicated/Private, customers can run the purge themselves against their buckets; we supply CLI/answers and review if requested.

4) SOC2: We are SOC2 Type II compliant (report available under NDA); additional compliance artifacts can be shared through our security portal.

Happy to provide the signed statement above on company letterhead if that helps Acme's risk team. Let me know and we will route it through Legal.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
